source.title: Hedonic Neurons: A Mechanistic Mapping of Latent Coalitions in Transformer MLPs
source.authors: Tanya Chowdhury; Atharva Nijasure; Yair Zick; James Allan

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies neuron coalitions in LoRA-fine-tuned rerankers, but does not measure pole-level interpretability, the stated shares of neurons with one or two jobs, or any of the other specific claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports outcomes for coalition-level synergy, ablation, and feature alignment. These are relevant to neuron interpretability broadly, but none measures the specific claims in V1–V7. The paper's discussion of individual neurons and polysemanticity is not a result about the stated claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study builds game-theoretic coalitions of MLP neurons in LoRA-fine-tuned rerankers (LLaMA-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, Pythia-6.9B). It reports coalition synergy, ablation drops, alignment with IR heuristics and cross-layer transitions. It never audits individual neurons for how many jobs they have. It does not score neuron explanations, analyse InceptionV1, build attribution graphs, or compare architectures or tools for interpretable-neuron shares. Its results do not bear on any version V1–V7. It motivates group-level analysis by citing polysemanticity, but has no result on it.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that hedonic coalitions are stable, synergistic, functionally indispensable and interpretable units that predict across domains. They add that most coalitions vanish or split across layers while merges are rare, and read this as MLPs acting as filters or refiners of features. They present coalitions as complementary to SAEs and single-neuron analysis.
record.recipe_differences: Uses hedonic-game coalition discovery with co-activation or ablation-based synergy in LoRA-fine-tuned rerankers; it does not audit neuron poles or test explanations on held-out activations.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper uses two coalition valuation methods, OCA and PAS, and reports task- and model-dependent results; it does not report sensitivity tests for the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Hedonic-PAS coalitions give 3–5× larger OOD ablation drops than clustering baselines (e.g. CQTR 0.11–0.14 vs ≈0.02–0.03). They also align far more strongly with IR heuristics (R² 0.55–0.67 vs ∼0.11–0.18).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In LoRA-fine-tuned rerankers, neuron groups selected for ablation synergy are more causally important, and more aligned with known IR features, than activation-clustering groups.

fits_no_version.finding: Compared with spherical k-means, hedonic coalitions have higher Pairwise synergy (average margin +0.29) and higher Ratio synergy (+0.49).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Game-theoretic coalition discovery recovers neuron groups with stronger non-additive interactions than activation-similarity clustering.

record.code_released: The paper says code, models, and datasets are provided with the submission; URL not stated.
record.problems: Evidence concerns LoRA-fine-tuned rerankers and scalar information-retrieval tasks, and evaluates neuron groups rather than human interpretability or single-neuron job counts. The authors also note that the analysis is layer-local and omits attention mechanisms and higher-order interactions.
record.rows_left_out: Coalition predictivity and cross-layer transition rates were not included because they do not directly bear on the claim's stated versions; see Section 4, Table 2, and Table 3.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or shares of one-job, two-job or unexplained neurons.
No per-neuron interpretability shares in any model. The models studied are 7–8B dense rerankers, and only their coalitions are analysed.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic-neuron reanalysis, and no test of recursive generalization versus superposition.
No comparison of interpretable-neuron shares across architectures, regularization or tools.
No attribution graphs and no comparison with replacement models or their reconstruction error.
No test of whether explanations fitted to activating examples predict where neurons fire.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6/discusses classification and its 'none' row links are correct. No row needs fixing. The feature-alignment R² is a coalition-level correlation with IR heuristics, not a per-neuron interpretability share, so it does not bear on V1, V2 or V4. The study does not test the claim, so it gets no verdict labels.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or counts of poles by number of jobs or not-yet-understood status.
No audit of single-neuron job shares across models, architectures, or scales.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron analysis or test of recursive generalization versus superposition.
No comparison of interpretable-neuron shares across architectures, tools, or regularization settings.
No attribution graphs or test of whether they explain behavior without a trained replacement model.
No comparison of explanations fitted to activating examples against predictions of where neurons fire.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations on new text.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-v0.1, and Pythia-6.9B (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Ablated a Hedonic-PAS coalition by restoring its neurons to their pre-LoRA state and measured OOD performance drop.
rows.measure: OOD performance drop from coalition ablation
rows.baseline: K-means/Hierarchical coalition drops: approximately 0.02–0.04, depending on task and model.
rows.value: Hedonic-PAS coalition drops: 0.11–0.17, depending on task and model.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ±95% confidence intervals across three seeds are reported in Table 1; uncertainty for the prose aggregate range is not stated.
rows.locator: Section 4, Table 1, and subsection 'Functional importance and interpretability'
rows.note: The prose summarizes results across the three models and tasks; this is coalition-level ablation evidence, not a test of single-neuron job counts.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-v0.1, and Pythia-6.9B (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared each coalition's mean activation with known IR heuristics using maximum squared Pearson correlation.

conditions.value: IR heuristics including BM25, IDF, and query-term coverage

rows.uncertainty: Mean ±95% confidence intervals across three seeds are reported in Table 1; uncertainty for the prose aggregate range is not stated.
rows.locator: Section 4, Table 1, and subsection 'Functional importance and interpretability'
rows.note: The aggregate range is reported across models, tasks, and clustering baselines. This measures coalition-to-heuristic alignment, not the interpretability of individual neurons.

rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals across three seeds are reported in Table 6; uncertainty for the average margin is not stated.
